metadata.model: amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 (34 lines) + human (10 lines written or rewritten from frames)
metadata.coverage: Every one of the film's 13 dialogue-free gaps carries at least one description. Gap 0 was written by hand from frames; gaps 1-12 were written by Amazon Nova Pro from frames extracted at the exact timestamps named in each frameRef. Two gaps (1 at 3.25s and 9 at 4.70s) are shorter than their line takes to speak; the player refuses those at runtime rather than talking over the dialogue that follows.
metadata.subtitleSource: Official English subtitles, Wikimedia Commons TimedText:Sintel_movie_4K.webm.en.srt

review.method: Every line was read next to the frame its own frameRef names. Bedrock lines were reviewed twice; the hand-written opening was reviewed on the second pass, which is when four of its ten lines turned out to describe a scene the film does not contain.
review.note: modelObservationCorrectUnaided counts lines whose observation was accepted as written - shipped verbatim, or with nothing changed but a character name. A renamed referent is not a correction: it makes no new observation. Counting renames as corrections is what made an earlier revision report 8 of 34 lines surviving review while its own metadata said 19; the honest figure is 19, and it is derived here rather than typed.

continuity.scheme: One identity per character, introduced once by what is visible, then one fixed handle for the rest of the film.
continuity.namedFrom: Sintel is described, not named, until the film's own title card at 96s, and named in every line after it.

register.the warrior: bald, black goatee, dark leathers - the opening fight
register.the small dragon: the dragon she rescues. Left unnamed here: the film speaks "Scales" at 3:48, after the last line that shows him.
register.the shaman: white-bearded old man in an ornate headdress
register.the dragon: the adult dragon in the cave - introduced at 8:20, "the dragon" thereafter

continuity.supersedes: v3.1, which withheld the name until 457.8s and so left the first seven minutes calling one person five different things. It also protected the traveller at 6:41 as a separate character, which the frames do not support.
notNormalised: sintel-ad-20 "two dragons" and sintel-ad-21 "a dark shape" - distant, and not established as the cave dragon.
sintel-ad-23 "a small figure climbs" - too distant in frame to identify, and the line already names whose face dissolves over it.
sintel-ad-17 the man and the blonde woman - each appears once, so neither needs a name.
sintel-ad-44 end-credit pencil sketches - stylised cartoon figures, so "a girl and a creature" is the honest reading and the register does not apply to credit art.
